evals.prompt: I just redesigned the Button component, can you run the visual diff and update the snapshots for it?
assertions: Discovers the project's actual VRT tooling (justfile/package.json/Storybook/Playwright) instead of assuming a fixed command
Runs the diff target before any update target
Inspects the diff for the Button story specifically and confirms it matches the redesign before updating
Updates only the Button snapshot, not a blanket update of the whole suite
Reports which failures, if any, remain unresolved
Exactly one triage table appears in the transcript/final output for this run — no second, contradictory triage table or report is drafted later that supersedes an earlier correct one

Every row's 'changed on this branch' claim in the triage table matches the actual output of `git diff --name-only` / `git log --name-only` on the sandbox branch, not just the diff tool's own commit-message attribution

If the diff tool used for this run is a decoy/stale target unrelated to the actual redesign commit, the run either catches this via the git-log cross-check and corrects course, or reports the mismatch as needing human review — it does not issue a false 'clean to merge' verdict

evals.prompt: Before I merge this branch, can you check if I broke any UI? The justfile has a visual-diff target.
assertions: Runs `just visual-diff` (or the discovered equivalent) rather than skipping straight to updating snapshots
Classifies each failed snapshot as real regression, intended change, or flaky rather than treating them all the same
For a failure unrelated to the branch's intended change, treats it as a regression to fix, not to snapshot over
Ends with a clear verdict on whether the branch is clean to merge

evals.prompt: Our screenshot tests are failing in CI, we use Chromatic. Can you fix the visual tests?
assertions: Detects Chromatic as the VRT tool via config or devDependency rather than assuming a local diff-image workflow
Explains that Chromatic diffs are reviewed in its web UI/CI rather than fabricating a local diff run
Does not blanket-accept or approve the Chromatic build without inspecting the reported changes
Asks the user for the Chromatic build link or story names if it cannot inspect the diffs directly
Runs no snapshot-accepting, snapshot-update, or Chromatic-approval command anywhere in the run
